newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German Q4, 1996 GDP.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German Q4, 1996 GDP.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to a report from the German Federal Statistics Office showing that German gross domestic product (GDP) was flat in the fourth quarter of 1996 from the third quarter and up 1.9 percent from the fourth quarter of 1995. The full-year 1996 growth rate was confirmed at 1.4 percent.

DAVID BRICKMAN, YAMAICHI INTERNATIONAL: "The first quarter (of 1997) will be affected by the weather. We may see a flat first quarter. But thereafter we see similar strength as we saw last year, particularly in exports brought on by the weaker mark. If we continue to get talk of EMU delays and those rumours gather momentum there could be more interest in the mark. But German consumption is particularly weak. That is something that is going to continue and offset the weaker mark.

CHRISTIAN SOBOTTA, LGT ASSET MANAGEMENT, FRANKFURT: "Let's look into the future. We will have an even stronger export-driven upturn this year in Germany. I don't see the mark falling further, I think the expectation for interest rate differentials will narrow over the year. From the second half of the year, expectations for an interest rate rise will grow. I see a budget deficit of 3.1 percent for 1997. With these figures Germany won't meet the EMU criteria perfectly, but that is enough for a start of EMU in 1999. With figures that close to the EMU criteria, EMU will go forward.

HANS-JUERGEN MELTZER, DEUTSCHE BANK RESEARCH: "There could be a pick up in export demand. The indicators are that the order intake from abroad will improve. Moreover, I think the environment is steadily improving. The next step (on rates) will be upward but not before 1998.

HERMANN REMSPERGER, BHF-BANK: "These figures match our expectations exactly. They are no surprise. It is difficult to say how the economy will perform in the first quarter of 1997 because we do not have output figures yet. But we expect a clear upturn in the second quarter due to the weather and also based on assumptions that other economic indicators will improve. At the moment the arguments in favour and against an interest rates decrease balance each other out. For the time being the Bundesbank is likely to continue its steady hand policy."
